newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian incumbents lose top party posts.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian incumbents lose top party posts.

text.p: Malaysia's feisty International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz on Wednesday narrowly lost the chairmanship of the women's wing of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's political party.

In another closely watched battle, the incumbent chairman of the youth wing of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), Rahim Tamby Chik, lost to a political newcomer and chairman of a state bank.

Rafidah Aziz, a former economics professor who had headed the women's wing of the UMNO for the past decade, lost to Deputy Health Minister Siti Zaharah Sulaiman by 271 to 244, according to an official tally.
Rahim placed third in his race, losing to Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, the UMNO youth information chief and chairman of Bank Simpanan Nasional.
Hishamuddin Tun Hussein, son of the late former prime minister Hussein Onn, was elected deputy chairman of the youth wing.

Both Rafidah and Rahim were contesting under a cloud of corruption allegations at a time when Mahathir has made "money politics" -- which encompasses a host of sins, including vote buying -- the central issue of the triennial party polls.
This was the first time that Rafidah was challenged since taking over as head of the women's wing in 1984.

She was cleared by the Attorney General's office last year of any wrongdoing after she chaired a meeting which allocated shares in a publicly-listed company to her son-in-law under a system favouring indigenous Malay entrepreneurs.
Her opponent made it an issue, when she announced her challenge some six months ago.
A tearful Rafidah told reporters she was going ahead with a trade mission to Europe next week. "Maybe in Europe they'll see that the minister was not acknowledged by (her) own women."

Losing her party job does not mean Rafidah has to leave the cabinet, political analysts said. In the 1993 UMNO elections, Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi lost his vice presidential race, but kept the foreign ministry portfolio.
Rahim, who was not favoured to win, was philosophical in defeat. "I receive with full acceptance the decision. In all contests there are winners and losers," he told reporters.

A former chief minister of the west coast state of Malacca, Rahim won the youth chief's post in the 1993 but was forced to step down from both jobs last year after he was charged in court on two counts of corruption. That followed a police investigation into a complaint that he had sex with an underaged schoolgirl.

He was acquitted on the corruption charges and never prosecuted on the sexual allegation. Mahathir strongly defended Rahim at the time, saying he was being tried in the press. Rahim, with Mahathir's blessing, became the head of the youth wing again last January.

Analysts said UMNO's triennial elections are more significant than Malaysia's general elections as by political convention the president and deputy president of the party become prime minister and deputy prime minister.
Important positions in UMNO also usually lead to top jobs in government and access to business opportunities.
Neither Mahathir nor his deputy Anwar Ibrahim are being challenged for the top two posts in this year's polls.

But analysts see the 49-year-old Anwar as anxious to succeed the 70-year-old Mahathir and all contests in the elections are viewed as a battle between proxies of the two. Rafidah and Rahim are both staunch allies of the prime minister.
